response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan AS timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT AVG(match_count) AS avg_n FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(g.match_count) AS total_match_count, AVG(g.match_count - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.match_count > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: Match count for a group is the number of joined fee-order rows (COUNT(*)) in that time-in-force group; recordvault is assumed unique in orders so the join doesn't duplicate fees.
The cross-group average match count is the simple average of per-group counts (each group weighted equally), and a NULL timespan, if present, is treated as its own group.
Rows where feerate is 0 or NULL, or rebrate is NULL, yield a NULL ratio (SQLite returns NULL on division by zero) and are ignored by AVG, though they still count as matches.
